Section.name: Executive Summary
Section.Content: FirmOS is an autonomous, multi-agent AI development environment modeled after a corporate organizational chart. Instead of a single monolithic prompt, FirmOS utilizes specialized, ephemeral AI agents (defined by Markdown system prompts) that communicate asynchronously via a message broker (RabbitMQ). Agents operate using "Native Tool Calling" to read, write, and explore the local filesystem to complete complex software development lifecycles (SDLC).

Subsection.name: The 'Shared Brain' Directory Structure
Subsection.Content: Agent identities (System Prompts) are decoupled from target projects. FirmOS acts as the universal engine.
Subsection.CodeBlock: * FirmOS/ (The Orchestrator) * .env (Contains GEMINI_API_KEY) * package.json (amqplib, @google/generative-ai, dotenv) * src/ * daemon.js (The core engine / message consumer) * publish.js (Ticket creator) * scripts/tickets/ (JSON task payloads) * company/roles/ (Nested Agent Personas) * hr/hr-director.md * product/product-manager.md * engineering/backend-architect.md * engineering/frontend-developer.md

Subsection.name: Macro-Loops vs. Micro-Loops
Subsection.Content: The fundamental execution model relies on two distinct loops to balance autonomy with cost-control.

List.ListItem: Macro-Loops (Inter-Agent Handoffs): Managed by RabbitMQ. A ticket represents a massive unit of work (e.g., "Draft System Architecture"). When an agent finishes a macro-task, the Daemon acks the message and publishes the next phase to the next department's queue.

Micro-Loops (Intra-Agent Tool Use): Managed by the Daemon's `while` loop. While processing a single queue ticket, an agent can take multiple autonomous actions (e.g., Read a file -> Analyze -> Read another file -> Save a file). The Daemon intercepts these tool calls, executes the Node.js `fs` commands, and feeds the results back into the same chat session. Micro-loops are hard-capped (e.g., MAX_LOOPS = 5) to prevent runaway token burn.

Section.name: The Toolchain (Native Function Calling)
Section.Content: Agents interact with the environment exclusively through strict JSON schema function calls injected into the Gemini API context. Currently Implemented Tools:

List.ListItem: `save_file`: Writes string content to a specified relative path. (Creates directories if they don't exist).
`read_file`: Returns the text content of a specified relative path.
`list_directory`: Returns an array of files and folders at a specified relative path.

Section.name: The Orchestrator Daemon (src/daemon.js)
Section.Content: The heart of FirmOS. Its responsibilities are:

List.ListItem: Connect to RabbitMQ (`task_routing` and `error_tasks` queues).
Consume a JSON ticket `{ "role": "hr-director", "prompt": "..." }`.
Read the corresponding Markdown system prompt from `company/roles/`.
Initialize a `gemini-3-flash-preview` Chat Session with the `firmOsTools` array.
Send the prompt and enter the Micro-Loop Engine.
Execute requested `functionCalls` (fs.readFile, fs.writeFile, etc.) and return the data to the model.
Terminate the loop when the model outputs raw text instead of a tool call, or hits `MAX_LOOPS`.
`ack` the message on success, or route to `error_tasks` on fatal failure (404, 401, missing files).

Section.name: Agent Prompts (The SLAs)
Section.Content: Every agent in `company/roles/` MUST adhere to a strict structure. They are essentially Service Level Agreements (SLAs) dictating data in/data out. Required Sections in every Markdown Role:

List.ListItem: ROLE: Title and core purpose.
CONTEXT: Functional position in the macro-workflow.
CAPABILITIES: Explicitly mention Native Tool Calling (`save_file`, `read_file`, etc.).
INPUT: The exact format/schema expected from the upstream agent.
OUTPUT FORMAT: Strict rules on how to format the tool arguments or final output.
CONSTRAINTS: Strict prohibitions (e.g., "Do not write backend code", "Do not loop endlessly").
Verify the Engine: Run the daemon locally and use the HR Director to hire the `backend-architect.md` using the `save_file` tool.
Test File Reading: Create a dummy project spec (`docs/raw-idea.txt`). Issue a ticket to the Architect to `read_file` on the raw idea, and `save_file` an architecture document.

Queue Expansion: Update `daemon.js` to handle multiple distinct queues (e.g., `hr_queue`, `engineering_queue`) instead of a single `task_routing` queue, allowing for true asynchronous department handoffs.
